ideas.pitch: An AI-driven defense-in-depth security proxy that hardens web applications against prompt injections and automated exploitation agents in real-time.
ideas.title: AgentShield CTF
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly applies the winning pattern of defense-in-depth and prompt-injection hardening from the BitGN Personal Agent Challenge to realistic CTF web challenges.

ideas.pitch: An automated cryptographic puzzle solver and frequency analysis suite tailored for rapid flag retrieval in CTF crypto challenges.
ideas.title: CryptoSleuth
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targets the high-speed execution needed in 24-hour CTF competitions by automating common RSA and cipher attacks.

ideas.pitch: An automated OSINT investigation tool that aggregates social footprints, metadata, and geolocation data to rapidly solve digital forensics challenges.
ideas.title: OSINT-Map
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses heavily on the digital forensics and OSINT domains explicitly highlighted in the Seize da Flaq competition description.

ideas.pitch: A BERT-powered email, SMS, and call-log analysis platform designed to detect advanced social engineering attacks and extract embedded flags.
ideas.title: PhishGuard CTF
ideas.why_it_could_win: Reuses proven architecture from the Cyber Hackathon runner-up project, adapting it for security analysis tracks.

ideas.pitch: A zero-knowledge proof gating system that allows players to prove they found a CTF flag without revealing the flag string itself to teammates or opponents.
ideas.title: ZK-FlagVault
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages advanced ZK circuits which consistently win technical engineering tracks at competitive hackathons.
